title: Business Rules & Client Scripts

sections.heading: Business Rules (server)
sections.content: A Business Rule runs server-side during database operations on a table. Types: before (before the write, can modify/abort), after (after the write, e.g. notifications), async (asynchronous, does not block the user), display (runs when the form loads, transfers data to the client).

sections.heading: Client Scripts (browser)
sections.content: A Client Script runs in the browser. Types: onLoad (when the form loads), onChange (when a field changes), onSubmit (on submission, can block the submit), onCellEdit (inline editing in a list).

sections.heading: UI Policies vs scripts
sections.content: UI Policies let you make a field mandatory, visible, or read-only in a declarative way (no code), and are preferred over Client Scripts for these simple cases. The 'Order' field determines the execution order between rules/scripts of the same type.

pieges: Using a Client Script to enforce a security rule: critical validation must always be duplicated server-side (Business Rule/ACL).
Confusing 'before' and 'after': modifying current in an 'after' Business Rule does not prevent the write that has already happened.
Writing a complex Client Script when a UI Policy would be enough to make a field visible/mandatory.
